comment: Lines of fixtures/text/extracted.json where an extractor does not return the text lamina drew, each with the extractor behaviour behind it and a link to the upstream code (todos B4b, B4d). crates/laminapdf-text/tests/extraction.rs requires every other line to equal the input and every entry here to still match the facts.

exceptions.reason: pdf.js rebuilds spaces from the gaps between glyphs and drops whitespace glyphs; a right-to-left line of several runs (Hebrew words around a comma from Noto Sans) is drawn in logical order, right to left, and at each backward move to the next run pdf.js resets its last-characters state and starts a new text item, so the space at the run boundary is lost (drawn in visual order instead, the items come out in visual order)

exceptions.extracted: नमस्ते दु निया। हिन्दी पाठ का परीक्षण कर्म
exceptions.reason: pdf.js treats a glyph whose text contains a nonspacing mark anywhere as a zero-width diacritic (getCharUnicodeCategory's /^(\s)|(\p{Mn})|(\p{Cf})$/u leaves the Mn alternative unanchored), so the दु ligature (one spacing glyph standing for द + U+0941) neither advances nor checks its position, and the space before it is emitted after it

pypdf turns a TJ number of at least half a space into a space appended to the current text, while it builds right-to-left text by prepending; the Hebrew points are positioned with such numbers, so a space lands at the logical end of the pointed run
pdftotext writes right-to-left text as it is displayed: phrases in visual order, each wrapped in U+202B…U+202C embeddings, not in logical order
pdftotext writes right-to-left text in display order inside U+202B…U+202C embeddings and splits words at the Hebrew points' offsets

exceptions.extracted: The words ‫ שלום עולם‬and ‫ مرحبا بالعالم‬mean hello.
exceptions.reason: pdftotext wraps each right-to-left phrase of the mixed line in U+202B…U+202C embeddings, moving the space after it inside, before the phrase
pdftotext drops the spaces of the non-embedded ZapfDingbats line (its word segmentation treats the symbolic font's glyphs as one word); pypdf and pdf.js read them
